title: repo-manifest.yml
description: Validates the repository-root repo-manifest.yml. Enforced by scripts/validate-manifests.py in `make check`, which also asserts that every required path exists on disk. This is the file that stops the pack quietly shrinking: a deleted document fails the build rather than disappearing, and a path promised for a later phase stays visible as a debt rather than being forgotten.

current_phase.description: The highest build phase considered complete. Required paths from later phases are reported as pending rather than failing, so this manifest can be authored once, up front, as a plan the build is measured against. Raising this number turns on more required paths, which is the only way the plan tightens.

path.description: Repository-relative. A trailing slash means directory.

why.description: What breaks if this path is missing. A required path with no stated consequence is a preference, and preferences do not belong in a gate.

phase.description: The build phase that creates it. Paths from later phases are reported as pending rather than failing, so the manifest can be authored once up front.

min_bytes.description: Guards against the empty-file dodge: a path that exists but says nothing.

min_files.description: For a directory: how many files with content it must hold, ignoring placeholders such as .gitkeep. Defaults to 1, so an empty directory never satisfies a required path. Raise it where a directory is only meaningful with several members, such as a theme that needs both a template and its specimen.

pattern.description: A Python regular expression searched across every tracked text file.

allow_in.description: Glob paths where the pattern is legitimate, because the pack has to be able to discuss a credential file in order to tell readers not to mount one. Machine-readable on purpose: a prose exception is an exception nothing enforces.

harness_placeholders.description: The harnesses that are labelled rather than implemented. Machine-readable so that 'this directory contains no configuration' is a checked property and not a promise in a README: the failure mode is a half-finished renderer leaving a loadable config next to a STATUS.md that still says the harness is unsupported.

root.description: Directory the named placeholders live under.

allowed_files.description: The complete set of filenames permitted in a placeholder directory. Anything else is a failure, because the point of the check is that no file here can be loaded by a harness.

min_bytes.description: Floor for each allowed file. A placeholder whose STATUS.md says only 'coming soon' is the thing this section exists to prevent.

directories.description: Each must also appear in PLACEHOLDERS in harness/scripts/render.py. The cross-check is the point: the directory's emptiness and the renderer's refusal are two halves of one claim and drift apart silently when only one is edited.
